messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: advice on RS-DBI connections
parts:
I've been struggling to come up with a good solution to maintain a database connection that can be reused across sessions without opening too many connections.  Declaring and opening the connection at the server level (outside session scope) seems to work fine, but then the connection times out overnight; if the sessions have to check the connection, and possibly replace it (using <<-), then I'm worried about a race condition between concurrent sessions (should I be?).  Previously I was having each session open a new connection, and then close it when finished, but when developing/debugging (read: errors), the connections would not get closed, and eventually I'd have to restart the server ("too many connections" error from RS-DBI).

Advice?

Thanks,
-Aaron

Wow, you'd have to restart the server? Are you sure just restarting the R process wouldn't fix it? If the latter is true, then perhaps you could write your own wrapper around shiny::runApp that would wrap it in a withCallingHandlers call, and in the case of exception, close the connection.

BTW, how were you able to tell when a Shiny session is finished?

messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
parts:
How do I restart the R process without restarting the shiny-server?  Reloading the page reloads the server.R code, but doesn't restart the R process (?)

Regardless, how should I orchestrate things to keep from having to restart anything?

re: <<- and race conditions -- is this a general concern? said another way, are individual sessions run in parallel threads, or only serially (new sessions "block" or wait until earlier session responses are completed)?  It's not clear to me what the UML sequence diagram looks like with stateful websockets ...

and no, I don't know when a session finishes; what I meant to say is that I previously had each function that needed a connection open a new one, and close it when finished; but errors in between caused orphaned connections to be left open.  I could clean up my database access routines to use tryCatch to more cleanly exit without leaving orphans, but it still seems wasteful to constantly re-open database connections, when one "master" connection should suffice -- if I could just keep it from timing out (a RS-DBI question, I suppose).

-Aaron

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
parts:
Oh, I misunderstood. I thought you meant you had to restart the database server.

All R code in a process runs single-threaded. This is just an inherent feature/limitation of R itself. So you should be able to structure your code so that race conditions are not too much of a concern. Probably the easiest thing to do then would be to create a function in global.R that does something like the following:

getConnection <- function() {
  if (!exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv) || (Sys.time() - .connOpened) > 600) {
    if (exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv))
      closeConnection(.connection)
    .connection <<- openNewConnection()
    .connOpened <<- Sys.time()
  }
  return(.connection)
}

Basically it returns a cached connection, unless a certain amount of time has passed, in which case it closes the existing connection and opens a new one. Or instead of basing it on time, you could run a trivial query and see if it succeeds.

messages.author: bff9e4feca8b059f
messages.subject: Re: advice on RS-DBI connections
parts:
Here's what I ended up with in global.R

library(RMySQL)

getConnection <- function(group) {

  if (!exists('.connection', where=.GlobalEnv)) {
    .connection <<- dbConnect(MySQL(), group=group)
  } else if (class(try(dbGetQuery(.connection, "SELECT 1"))) == "try-error") {
    dbDisconnect(.connection)
    .connection <<- dbConnect(MySQL(), group=group)
  }

  return(.connection)
}

Thanks again,
-Aaron
